t: Maximum Strength of K Disjoint Subarrays
o: Pick exactly k disjoint, ordered subarrays; the i-th contributes ±(k−i+1)·sum(sub_i) with alternating signs starting positive (odd k guarantees the last coefficient is +1). We maximize the total. In Example 1 (k=3) coefficients are +3,−2,+1 and the best choice [1,2,3],[−1],[2] yields 3·6 −2·(−1) + 2 = 22. In Example 2, k = n forces singletons, giving 64. In Example 3 with k = 1 we must pick some subarray, so even all-negative input forces a negative answer (−1). Constraints allow n·k ≤ 10⁶, strongly hinting at an O(n·k) DP. Subarrays must be non-empty and appear in order.
k: Process elements left to right tracking (number of subarrays finished, whether the current element extends the last subarray) — a classic 'exactly k segments' DP.
The signed coefficient of segment j is c_j = (−1)^(j+1)·(k−j+1); fold it in as soon as a segment starts, since extending by one element changes the strength by c_j·nums[i].

a.n: Approach 1: Bottom-up segment DP with prefix-friendly transitions
a.i: Let dp[j][i] be the best strength using exactly j completed subarrays within the first i elements (subarrays may end anywhere ≤ i), and cur[j][i] the best strength where the j-th subarray ends exactly at i. Element i either extends the j-th subarray (cur[j][i] = max(cur[j][i−1], dp[j−1][i−1]) + c_j·nums[i−1]) or is skipped (dp[j][i] = max(dp[j][i−1], cur[j][i])). Because dp[0][i] = 0, every transition is well-defined, and folding c_j per element avoids needing explicit prefix sums in the recurrence.
s: Initialize dp[0][i] = 0 for all i; everything else −∞.
For j = 1..k with coefficient c_j, sweep i = 1..n: cur[j][i] = max(cur[j][i−1], dp[j−1][i−1]) + c_j·nums[i−1]; dp[j][i] = max(dp[j][i−1], cur[j][i]).
a.t: O(n·k) — each of the k layers sweeps n positions once; fits the n·k ≤ 10⁶ budget.
a.sp: O(n·k) for the two DP tables (reducible to O(n) with rolling rows).

w: This DP is the intended solution; in an interview, first state the 'exactly k ordered segments' framing and the per-element coefficient trick, then code the two-table sweep. Pitfalls: mixing up the sign convention (coefficient of segment j is +(k−j+1) for odd j, negative for even j), forgetting subarrays must be non-empty (guaranteed by starting segments from dp[j−1][i−1]), and 64-bit overflow in C++/Java (use long long/long). Follow-ups: what if subarrays could overlap, or coefficients were arbitrary — the same layered DP adapts by changing c_j.
